Evidence first.
Always.

What belongs here?

Research with a substantive AI method or AI application and a central medical, biomedical, bioinformatics or biological-discovery task. Clinical medicine, molecular and cellular biology, omics, protein design, drug discovery and related biomedical engineering are in scope. Pure medicine without AI and general AI papers with only incidental biomedical examples are excluded.

Which journals and dates?

Nature, Nature-branded research and review journals, Nature Communications, and npj Digital Medicine. Other npj journals and the separate Communications series are outside this snapshot. Records begin on 1 January 2026 and run through the snapshot date in the coverage ledger. Journal families are navigation categories, not a quality ranking or an assertion of indexing status.

How are scale, data and institutions verified?

Sample sizes retain their units and cohort roles. Patients, visits, images, cells and datasets are not added together. First-institution statistics use an explicit publisher author-to-affiliation mapping and count each paper once. Dataset and resource links point to the paper’s original availability statements. Fields that are not stated in accessible evidence are identified rather than inferred.

How should I read the statistics?

Charts describe indexed articles in the current selection. They are not estimates of the complete biomedical AI share of a journal. Themes can overlap, incomplete recall can affect time trends, and publication counts are not measures of research quality. Research articles and reviews retain their publisher article types. A review does not have a new experimental cohort.
